1.why: verify-reset requires the token hash to match session.resetTokenHash and token.sessionId/accountId, so the code must belong to that user/session.

2.why: Reset tokens are bound to sessionId and accountId and fail verification for any other session/user, so the claim is false.

3.why: reset-password never invalidates other sessions; only the current grant is consumed, so prior sessions keep working.

4.why: Bun.serve is configured with TLS cert/key, HSTS, and HTTP→HTTPS redirect, though the TLS version is not explicitly pinned in code.

5.why: Reset tokens and emails are SHA-256 hashed and passwords bcrypt-hashed; not classical encryption, but appropriate crypto protection is used.

6.why: No real email body is built; responses use a generic privacy-neutral message and do not echo private account fields.

7.why: Emails/passwords/tokens are validated and length-limited, passwords hashed, and the client only inserts textContent.

8.why: Redirects use fixed CONFIGURED_HTTPS_ORIGIN only after Host checks; client recovery links are same-origin paths.

9.why: There are no server email templates that embed user input; delivery is a simulated JSON field only.

10.why: API errors are generic, but testToken and testMfaCode are returned and written into the on-page log list.

11.why: Initial password bcrypt hash and the fixed MFA value "246810" are embedded in source; only runtime password updates are bcrypt-hashed.

12.why: Sign-in MFA is always the hardcoded code 246810, which functions as a default credential in this flow.

13.why: Wrong reset verifications lock after 5 tries, reset requests are rate-limited, and MFA fails after 5 attempts.

14.why: request-reset always returns the same generic message and token shape whether or not the email matches.

15.why: Tokens come from secureToken(32) (cryptographic random base64url) and are stored/verified as user- and session-specific hashes.
